corpus.title: Magnitude 5.9 earthquake jolts eastern Japan, injuring over 20 people
corpus.signal_text:
Aamir Latif
23 August 2026•Update: 23 August 2026
A magnitude 5.9 earthquake struck eastern Japan early Sunday, injuring more than 20 people and disrupting transportation, local media reported, citing the country’s weather agency and local authorities.
No tsunami alert was issued after the quake, which originated in the southern part of Ibaraki prefecture at a depth of 68 kilometers (42 miles), Tokyo-based Kyodo News reported, quoting the Japan Meteorological Agency.
The tremor registered lower 5 on the Japanese seismic intensity scale of 7 in parts of the prefecture as well as in central Tokyo.
More than 20 people were injured, including a young man and a woman in her 70s in Saitama, north of Tokyo, as well as nine people in Kanagawa and four in Chiba prefectures.
Several train services were delayed following the quake, while some trains ran at reduced speeds.
Some express services operated by Tobu Railway remained halted.
An intensity of lower 5 was also recorded in parts of Saitama and Chiba prefectures and central Tokyo.
No abnormalities were detected at the Tokai No. 2 nuclear power plant in Ibaraki prefecture or the disaster-stricken Fukushima Daiichi nuclear plant and the nearby Fukushima Daini plant in northeastern Japan.
Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi instructed officials to ascertain the extent of the damage from the quake and provide timely information to the public.
The weather agency urged the public to remain alert for an earthquake registering lower 5 on the seismic intensity scale over the next week, especially during the next two to three days.
The latest quake was felt across a wide swath of the country, including northeastern and central Japan.

corpus.title: Magnitude 5.9 quake jolts Tokyo, triggers alerts across Japan
corpus.signal_text:
Magnitude 5.9 quake jolts Tokyo, triggers alerts across Japan
				
				
					
The latest quake was one of the strongest earthquakes to hit the Kanto region in recent weeks.
				
		
				 
				
					
TOKYO: A magnitude 5.9 earthquake struck southern Ibaraki on early Sunday, Aug. 23, shaking Tokyo and large parts of the Kanto region, triggering emergency alerts and causing strong jolts across several prefectures, but officials said there was no tsunami threat.
The earthquake occurred at a depth of roughly 70 kilometers, according to the Japan Meteorological Agency. The strongest shaking reached lower 5 on Japan’s seven level seismic intensity scale in parts of Ibaraki, Saitama, Chiba and Tokyo.
Tokyo’s 23 wards experienced noticeable shaking, with some areas recording an intensity of 4. The tremor was also felt across Tochigi, Gunma, Kanagawa and other nearby areas.
The quake triggered emergency alerts on mobile phones and other warning systems, giving residents an early warning as the shaking spread through the region. Japan’s Meteorological Agency urged people to remain cautious about possible aftershocks in the days ahead.
At least 37 people were injured across several prefectures, according to reports, with most injuries described as minor. Some people were hurt after being startled awake and falling or colliding with furniture. One elderly woman in Yokohama suffered a serious hip injury.
The earthquake also affected transportation in the Tokyo area. Several express trains were delayed, while Shinkansen bullet train services were not significantly affected, according to reports. Authorities also reported no irregularities at nuclear power plants.
The Japan Tourism Agency recommends its safety tips app for visitors and residents who want earthquake and tsunami alerts. The app provides emergency notifications, evacuation guidance and information about shaking across Japan.
The latest quake was one of the strongest earthquakes to hit the Kanto region in recent weeks. Authorities continue to monitor the situation as residents remain alert for possible aftershocks.

corpus.title: Sismo de 5.9 despierta a Japón: Reportan 37 heridos y alertan por otro posible temblor moderado (VIDEOS)
corpus.signal_text:
TOKIO (AP) — Un sismo de magnitud 5.9 sacudió el domingo el este de Japón, incluida el área metropolitana de Tokio, hiriendo a más de 30 personas, la mayoría de ellas levemente, dijeron autoridades. No había peligro de tsunami.
Según la Agencia Meteorológica de Japón, el sismo tuvo su epicentro en la prefectura sureña de Ibaraki, a una profundidad de 70 kilómetros (42 millas). El Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos cifró la magnitud en 5.8.
Al menos 37 personas resultaron heridas en cinco prefecturas de la región —15 en Tokio, nueve en Saitama, ocho en Kanagawa, cuatro en Chiba y una en Ibaraki—, según funcionarios locales y la Agencia de Gestión de Incendios y Desastres.
La mayoría resultaron heridas cuando se cayeron o se golpearon contra muebles o puertas al ser sorprendidos por el sismo mientras dormían y se levantaron de la cama en pánico, dijeron autoridades.
El sismo causó retrasos en los trenes exprés que brindan servicio a Tokio y al Aeropuerto de Narita, y en otros trenes locales en las regiones del noreste, pero los trenes bala Shinkansen funcionaban con normalidad, dijo su operador, East Japan Raiway Co.
Japón evalúa daños tras sismo y activa alerta por nuevas réplicas
El gobierno estableció un grupo de trabajo para evaluar el alcance de los posibles daños, indicó en X la primera ministra Sanae Takaichi.
La Agencia Meteorológica de Japón instó a los residentes en el área a tener precaución ante otro posible sismo moderado durante aproximadamente una semana.
El sismo también activó alertas de terremoto en teléfonos móviles y sacudió significativamente Tokio. La televisora pública NHK mostró que el tráfico en las calles de ciudades cercanas, incluidas Mito y Saitama, parecía normal.
Una tubería subterránea de agua se rompió en el distrito oriental de Koto, en Tokio, y el líquido se derramó sobre la calle, según imágenes de NHK. La tubería fue reparada y la fuga se detuvo más tarde.
No hubo reportes de nada fuera de lo normal en cerca de una docena de plantas nucleoeléctricas y otras instalaciones que manejan materiales nucleares, informó la Autoridad de Regulación Nuclear.
El mes pasado, un sismo de magnitud 7.1 sacudió el área de Kumamoto, en Kyushu, la isla más meridional de Japón, y causó la muerte de 38 personas y dejó 364 heridas.

corpus.title: Magnitude 5.9 earthquake near Tokyo injures at least 37
corpus.signal_text:
TOKYO, Aug 23 — A magnitude 5.9 earthquake struck near Tokyo early today, injuring at least 37 people and disrupting travel in the bustling megacity.
The quake caused violent shaking in the Japanese capital and its surrounding areas, prompting the nation’s warning systems to sound public announcements and sirens in the streets and lighting up smartphones with notices in affected areas.
The quake struck the southern part of the Ibaraki Prefecture near Tokyo at 2am (1700 GMT yesterday), the Japan Meteorological Agency said.
There were no concerns about a tsunami, the agency said, adding that the earthquake’s depth was 68 kilometres (42 miles).
The US Geological Survey estimated the strength at magnitude 5.8.
Japan’s Fire and Disaster Management Agency said that at least 37 people had suffered minor injuries.
The worst case was that of a woman in her 80s in Yokohama, south of Tokyo, who tried to leave her bed after the quake but fell and hurt her hip, according to the local government and media reports.
The late-night quake disrupted regional train services in Tokyo today morning, according to East Japan Railway Company.
A building in Saitama, north of Tokyo, also suffered minor damage, according to the Fire and Disaster Management Agency.
Authorities are investigating if a water main that ruptured in a neighbourhood in the capital was related to the quake, Kyodo News said.
The weather agency warned of an increased risk of landslides in the area as the quake could have loosened soil in the region, which was lashed by torrential downpours yesterday.
The agency also warned of the possibilitiy of strong aftershocks in the days ahead. — AFP
